narr: A slow moving low pressure system, along with plenty of moisture, allowed for showers and thunderstorms to gradually move through the Ohio Valley during the day on May 6th. Heavy rainfall occurred with these storms and additional storm and shower activity developed over the same areas. A swath of 3 to 4 inches of rain fell in a narrow corridor from Huntington northeastward to Elkins, with a few isolated pockets of 4 to 5 reported. This led to considerable flash flooding. A few stronger storms also developed, one of which led to an area of tree damage in Randolph County.||Multiple water rescues took place throughout the Metro Valley, including a man who was swept away while working on his tractor in Cabell County. Additionally, several vehicles were submerged in flood waters and over one hundred homes were impacted by high water with the hardest hit area being the Enslow Park community of Huntington. Flooding occurred across many roadways throughout West Virginia, leaving multiple roads impassable for a time until the water receded.||Even after the rain had concluded, several rivers in the state rose out of their banks for the next several days. This resulted in flooding along areas adjacent to the rivers.
ev: Flash floding occurred in several areas along 8th Street Road (Route 152) from Lavalette to the Cabell County line with water in several houses.

Significant flash flooding occurred in Cabell County. The hardest hit area was the Enslow Park area where over 100 homes and many vehicles were inundated as Fourpole Creek flooded. Some vehicles were swept away. Route 10 was closed due to flash flooding near Huntinton High School, Route 60 was impassable at the East Mall Road intersection in Barboursville, and flood waters entered Davis Creek Elementary School. A 63 year old man drowned in flood waters along Kilgore Creek Road in Milton. The man was working on a farm tractor and high water swept him away.

Flash flooding occurred throughout the county. Route 34 was impassable near City Park. High water flowed across Route 817 in multiple locations in Winfield and several neighborhoods also had high water across roads. A water rescue took place in Poca.

Widespread flash flooding occurred in Roane County. In Newton, high water affected the EMS Substation and the road leading to the station was impassable. Route 52 in Looneville was impassable. Amma Road was was impassable and multiple structures along the road were flooded. In Spencer, severel feet of water covered the intersection of Front Street and Market Street.

Several roads in the community of Sissonville, including Legg Fork Road, were affected by high water. A few of these roadways were closed due to flooding. Additionally, multiple water rescues occurred in Sissonville.
Multiple streets were flooded in St. Albans, including Kanawha Terrace, Greenbrier Street, the Boone Street Tunnel, and the 3rd Street Underpass. Woods Drive in Charleston also flooded.
High water flowed over portions of Six Mile Road as Six Mile Creek exceeded its banks.
Near the community of Branchland, Four Mile Creek Road became impassable due to flooding.
Flooding caused Bear Fork Road to become impassable near the community of Yawkey.
Summers Fork Road became impassable due to flooding.
Route 16 was closed in multiple locations across southern Calhoun County due to flooding.

Multiple roads were impassable due to flooding between the community of Fairplain and the Kanawha County line. These roadways included Charleston Road, Spicewood Road, Meadowview Drive, and Shamblin Run Road.
